CausalChain: Oncogenic miRNAs (eg, miR‐155) are transferred via exosomes → they downregulate tumor suppressor targets and promote EMT and drug resistance → Concurrently, reduced levels of tumor suppressor miRNAs (eg, miR‐128‐3p) fail to inhibit EMT and drug transporter expression (eg, Bmi1/MRP5) → This imbalance sustains a drug resistant, mesenchymal, and stem‐like state → Dual modulation via exosome‐mediated delivery of miR‐128‐3p mimics and blockade of miR‐155 re‐balances signaling to revert EMT and resensitize cancer cells to chemotherapy
Hypothesis: A dual‐exosome based therapeutic strategy that combines the exosomal delivery of miR‐128‐3p mimics with antagonism of miR‐155 will synergistically reverse EMT, reduce cancer stemness, and overcome chemoresistance in tumors such as lung, colorectal, or hepatocellular carcinoma.
Abstract: Emerging evidence underscores the pivotal role of microRNAs (miRNAs) in orchestrating the epithelial‐to‐mesenchymal transition (EMT) as well as in the acquisition of chemoresistance in many cancer types. Notably, exosomal transfer of miRNAs such as miR‐155 confers drug resistance by modulating EMT-related signaling, while tumor suppressive miRNAs such as miR‐128‐3p modulate drug uptake and EMT by targeting critical mediators of stemness and drug efflux. Here, we propose that a dual‐exosome therapeutic strategy that combines delivery of tumor suppressor miRNA mimics (eg, miR‐128‐3p) with inhibition of oncogenic miRNAs (eg, miR‐155) could synergistically reverse EMT, diminish cancer stem cell properties and restore chemosensitivity. This approach exploits the natural ability of exosomes to mediate intercellular communication and offers a novel avenue to re‐balance the miRNA milieu, ultimately disrupting the molecular circuits that promote drug resistance and metastasis in tumors.
